## TL;DR

Addressed the review findings for task #1070. Per-view skeletons no longer size themselves from collections that are empty precisely because the skeleton is showing. Those loading states now render one representative block, which is the smallest honest placeholder while the eventual collection size is unknown. Settings keeps its section count from `GENERAL_FIELD_SECTIONS`; Work and Inputs keep their lane counts from shared board constants. Skeletons now leave normal document flow as soon as their fade begins, preventing overlap with newly rendered page content from pushing the page down.

The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. Its remote run built the app, passed 365 test files (5,071 passed, one skipped), passed rendered contrast and UI smoke; local formatting, lint, build, CSS, and safety guards passed as well.

## Work and rationale

The review identified two related classes of bugs. First, several skeletons accepted a count from a page collection while their `loading` expression required that same collection to be empty. That binding could only produce zero, after which `PageSkeleton` fell back to one item. It looked like a data-driven count but was not. I removed those misleading count bindings across Checks, Check Runs, Reminders, Schedules, Model Providers, Agents, Releases, Deployments, Dev, and Secrets. The component’s representative-block fallback now describes these unknown-size collections directly. Settings still has a count the page knows before its content is drawn: the number of configured field sections. Board skeletons retain their shared lane constants, and the component still supports an explicit larger count where a caller has a reliable count.

Second, the per-view component used a leave opacity transition while its root stayed in normal flow. The page content was already rendering beneath it, so the placeholder’s delayed removal could change layout after content appeared. I made only the leave-transition element absolute and non-interactive. The entering skeleton remains in normal flow, preserving its initial layout reservation; the leaving skeleton fades over the real content without holding space. Reduced-motion CSS continues to disable animation and transition.

| Page / route | Real content layout | Skeleton layout after review fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Control `/` | One dashboard content block after the static heading | One dashboard block; no auto-fit card grid |
| Stories `/stories` | A single list region populated by visible stories | One representative row while the list is unknown |
| Work `/work` | Six board lanes from shared work-board constants | Six matching lanes; responsive CSS collapses lanes at the shared narrow breakpoint |
| Inputs `/inputs`, Client Board `/client-board` | Three input lanes from shared input-board constants | Three matching lanes; responsive collapse retained |
| Checks `/checks` plan | Plan controls followed by a tabular step list | One representative table row while plan data is absent |
| Check Runs | Run history table | One representative table row before history arrives |
| Releases `/releases` | Release summary cards and distribution channel cards | One representative card for each unknown first-load region |
| Deployments `/deployments` | Service groups plus a branch matrix | One representative service block and matrix row until status is known |
| Dev `/dev` | Configured target cards | One representative target card before targets arrive |
| Secrets `/secrets` | Environment key ledger/table | One representative table row until the snapshot arrives |
| Agents `/agents` | Agent cards, with detected agents in a row list | One representative card or detected-agent row while its source is loading |
| Settings `/settings` | Field sections and aligned setting rows | Section count follows `GENERAL_FIELD_SECTIONS`; rows remain grouped under those sections |
| Repo Context `/repo` and secondary routed pages | Document or detail content varies by route | Minimal row-style shell placeholder; it avoids suggesting a dense table or card grid |

The report table records the audited route shape and the chosen placeholder. It is intentionally conservative for data whose eventual count cannot be known before the response: a representative block occupies less space than a fabricated full collection and avoids a jump when data arrives. Static headings, tabs, and actions remain outside the placeholder.

Tests were changed from checking that source text contained count bindings to checking the component’s rendered item counts for each skeleton kind and known layout constants. Coverage includes one representative block per unknown-size kind, the Settings section count, an explicit 12-row table count, reduced motion, delayed/minimum shell timing, cached/fast loads, and the leave behavior/style contract. This makes a future count regression visible in rendered output rather than only in a regular-expression match.

## Approaches tried

I first considered keeping the collection bindings and changing the fallback arithmetic. That would preserve the misleading API contract and would still silently render a single row for an empty pre-load collection. Removing those bindings makes the state explicit: the page has no trustworthy count yet, so it gets one representative block. For counts that are available independently of the loading collection, the existing shared constants remain the source of truth.

For the transition, leaving the whole transition element in flow was the observed cause of the jump. Making the entering state absolute too would remove the initial layout reservation, so the positioning rule is limited to `.page-skeleton-leave-active`. Vue Test Utils stubs transition phases in this environment, so the regression test checks that the item is removed from the rendered tree and that the leave selector uses absolute positioning; the actual browser smoke gate also passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The first full remote check exposed two test defects, not product defects: one count assertion queried at the component wrapper instead of inside `.page-skeleton`, and a runtime assertion expected Vue Test Utils to retain a leave-transition class even though the test environment stubs the transition. I corrected the query and aligned the transition assertion with the behavior the test environment can observe. The focused loading-skeleton test then passed all 16 cases, and the later scoped remote check passed.

The first remote host timed out during validation and RepoOS retried on another host. The successful run completed normally; no code changes were needed in response to the host timeout. The worktree remained on the assigned branch and no `dist/` output was staged.

## Key learnings

A count binding is only meaningful when it is sourced independently from the data gate that decides whether the placeholder is visible. Unknown first-load collections should use a single illustrative row or block; counts that are knowable up front should come from the same constants the real layout uses. Transition leave behavior also needs to account for simultaneous rendering: opacity alone does not prevent the old placeholder from affecting layout during its fade. Finally, component tests should observe rendered counts and timing outcomes rather than merely asserting that a template contains a particular binding string.
